answer: A marketplace can require every agent to lock a refundable bond before bidding, then slash it when independent audits show that several identities coordinated to capture one scarce job. It tracks the delta in verified collusion and, over a rolling horizon, raises the minimum bond for new entrants; the attacker must fund every identity and risks forfeiting each deposit, making the cost of scaling exceed the likely payout. A quartz-sealed audit record prevents cheap re-entry under renamed accounts.
